extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting papers to NeurIPS 2021 / machine learning researchers preparing NeurIPS submissions
extracted.subtask_description: A conference checklist for NeurIPS 2021 authors to encourage best practices in reproducibility, transparency, research ethics, and societal impact when preparing submissions. It lists yes/no/n/a questions authors should answer and reference in their paper or supplemental material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist answering protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: You should answer yes, no, or n/a. You should reference the section(s) of the paper that provide support for your answer. You can also optionally write a short (1–2 sentence) justification of your answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are encouraged to take a look at the checklist early; reviewers will use the checklist as one factor in their evaluation. While "yes" is generally preferable, answering "no" or "n/a" is acceptable with proper justification (examples: computational cost, inability to find a dataset license). Supporting evidence can appear either in the main paper or the supplemental material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main claims reflect contributions and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper's contributions and scope?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should match theoretical and experimental results regarding generalization. Contributions and any important assumptions and limitations should be clearly stated. Aspirational goals may be included only if clearly identified as not attained by the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and conform to ethics review guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you read the ethics review guidelines and ensured that your paper conforms to them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are asked to read the ethics review guidelines referenced by NeurIPS and ensure conformity; this is a required-checklist prompt rather than a descriptive evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss potential negative societal impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss any potential negative societal impacts of your work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include malicious/unintended uses (disinformation, fake profiles, surveillance), environmental impact (training huge models), fairness considerations, privacy, and security (model/data stealing, adversarial attacks). Consider different stakeholders, especially vulnerable or marginalized communities, harms from intended correct use, incorrect outputs, and misuse. If negative impacts exist, discuss mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release, defenses, monitoring). Refer to provided unofficial guidance and broader impacts resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you describe the limitations of your work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to create a separate 'Limitations' section. Point out strong assumptions and robustness to violations (e.g., independence, noiseless settings, model misspecification, asymptotic approximations), reflect on scope of claims (datasets, number of runs), and factors influencing performance (e.g., low-resolution images harming facial recognition). Reviewers are instructed not to penalize honesty about limitations; use best judgement and be transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: State full set of assumptions for theoretical results
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you state the full set of assumptions of all theoretical results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. Authors are encouraged to discuss relationships between their results and related literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include complete proofs of theoretical results
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you include complete proofs of all theoretical results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs can appear in the main paper or supplemental material; if in supplemental, authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch in the main paper to provide intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide code, data, and instructions to reproduce experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you include the code, data, and instructions needed to reproduce the main experimental results (either in the supplemental material or as a URL)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce results. Main experimental results include new methods and baselines; try to capture as many minor experiments as possible. If only a subset is reproducible, state which ones. It is acceptable to answer 'no' if code/data are proprietary, but at submission time remember to release anonymized versions. See NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify training details
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you specify all the training details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full details can be provided with the code, but important details should be in the main paper so experiments are interpretable and reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report error bars / statistical significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you report error bars (e.g., with respect to the random seed after running experiments multiple times)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer 'yes' if you report error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests for your main experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report compute and resource usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you include the amount of compute and the type of resources used (e.g., type of GPUs, internal cluster, or cloud provider)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally provide compute required for individual experimental runs and total compute for the research project if possible. Authors are encouraged to use CO2 emissions trackers (experiment impact tracker, ML CO2 impact calculator, CodeCarbon) and provide that information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite creators of existing assets
rubrics_metrics.description: If your work uses existing assets, did you cite the creators?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset; state which version of the asset you're using and, if possible, include a URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify licenses of assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you mention the license of the assets?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) for each asset. If data was scraped, state copyright and terms of service for the source. If repackaging an existing dataset, state original and derived licenses. Use resources (e.g., paperswithcode) for license information and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include any new assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you include any new assets either in the supplemental material or as a URL?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During submission, anonymize assets (anonymized URL or anonymized zip). If you cannot release assets (proprietary), explicitly state the reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss consent for data collection/curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose data you're using/curating?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you collected data (e.g., crowdsourcing), include how instructions explained data usage. For existing datasets, check how data was collected and whether consent was obtained; try your best and report findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss presence of PII or offensive content in data
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss whether the data you are using/curating contains personally identifiable information or offensive content?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how you checked for PII or offensive content (e.g., scripts, manual sampling). Note that presence of such content is not automatically bad; the goal is to encourage discussion of undesirable properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include full participant instructions for human subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information can be in supplemental material, but if the main contribution involves human subjects, include as much detail as possible in the main paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe participant risks and IRB approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you describe any potential participant risks, with links to Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals, if applicable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe risks (e.g., exposure to offensive content, collection of PII) and provide IRB approval links if obtained. For initial submissions, avoid including information that would break anonymity (e.g., institution conducting the review). Participants should be warned where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report participant compensation (hourly wage and total spent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you include the estimated hourly wage paid to participants and the total amount spent on participant compensation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide amount paid for each task (including bonuses), discuss how task time was estimated, how wage was determined, and how you determined that it was fair.
